top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a symmetry-protected phase with an identifiable theoretical origin (Kane and Mele: the Z2 invariant and helical edge states) and a decisive experiment (Molenkamp's HgTe/CdTe edge-channel transport), with a stable interpretation after two decades of independent confirmation in several materials. The credit is incomplete because the HgTe proposal came from Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, so the citation must be narrow, confined to the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect. I accept this cost over P002, which is an excellent, reproduced and cleanly attributed measurement technology, but a new phase of matter outweighs a new accuracy regime and the second has not yet been redefined. P002 is a strong second, and I would not oppose it if the committee treats the attribution gap as disqualifying. Both are far better than no award.
